problems: stop 1 card 4, answer 1: copies a Prep line word for word

explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. David says, "I shall not want" (Psalm 23:1), which means he won't be short on what he needs. With the LORD as his shepherd, the sheep isn't left without. That's the idea of lacking here.

Not quite, baker. David never says he has to earn anything he needs. The LORD is the one who makes sure it's there, the way a shepherd takes care of his flock. Verse 1 names the LORD as the shepherd, and that's where the care comes from.
Not this one, baker. David doesn't say the LORD keeps him from losing anything. He does say he won't go without what he needs (Psalm 23:1), and that's the word that fits: lack.

Yes, baker. The LORD makes David lie down in green pastures and leads him beside quiet waters (Psalm 23:2). Lying down and drinking quiet water is what a sheep does when it's safe. David's picture is all about calm.

Not this one, baker. David doesn't work for these pastures or waters, and the text never says he's hustling. The LORD makes him lie down and leads him there (Psalm 23:2). The picture is rest, not effort.
Not this one, baker. Danger isn't in verse 2 at all. Here David is lying in green pastures beside quiet waters, with the LORD doing the leading (Psalm 23:2). Danger comes up later, in the valley.
Yes, baker. David says, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). The LORD's care goes deeper than grass and water, down to David's soul. That's the word for bringing something back to what it should be.

Not this one, baker. The verse says, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3), so the LORD is giving something back to David. Testing isn't in this line. Restores is the word, and it shows the shepherd's care.
Not quite, baker. The text says, "He restores my soul" (Psalm 23:3). Weighing a soul isn't in this psalm. Restores is the word, and it keeps the focus on the LORD doing the caring.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His name
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. David says the LORD guides him in the paths of righteousness "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). The reason the text gives is the LORD's own name, and that's the answer you found.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His flock
explanations.explanation: Not this one, baker. The sheep are the ones walking the path in this picture, but verse 3 gives the reason as "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3). The flock isn't the reason the text names.

explanations.answer: For the sake of His land
explanations.explanation: Not quite, baker. The land doesn't come up in verse 3. David says the LORD guides him in the paths of righteousness "for the sake of His name" (Psalm 23:3), and that's the reason the text names.

explanations.answer: Because the LORD is with him
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. David says, "for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4). Even in the valley of the shadow of death, the reason he gives for fearing no evil is the LORD being with him. He isn't claiming he's tough enough on his own.
Not this one, baker. David doesn't say he's strong enough by himself. He says, "for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4), and that's the reason he gives for fearing no evil. The LORD is the one with him.
Not quite, baker. The psalm never says the valley is short. David walks through it, and his reason for fearing no evil is "for You are with me" (Psalm 23:4).

Yes, baker. David says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me" (Psalm 23:4), in the same verse as the valley of the shadow of death. The rod and staff are the shepherd's tools, and David finds comfort in them while he's walking through that dark place.
Not this one, baker. David does say the LORD's rod and staff comfort him, and he says it in the same verse as the valley (Psalm 23:4). The text says, "Your rod and Your staff, they comfort me."
Yes, baker. David says, "You prepare a table before me" (Psalm 23:5). The LORD plays the host and David is the guest, so preparing a table is the host's part of the picture.
Not this one, baker. The verse says, "You prepare a table before me" (Psalm 23:5). A table is what the host sets out for a guest, and a tent isn't in this line.
Not quite, baker. Verse 2 talks about David lying down in green pastures (Psalm 23:2), but verse 5 says the LORD prepares a table before him. Bed isn't the word the text uses here.
Not this one, baker. David says the LORD prepares a table "in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). The enemies are right there in the picture, not off somewhere far away.
Yes, baker. David says the LORD prepares a table "in the presence of my enemies" (Psalm 23:5). The enemies are there in the scene, so the table isn't set far from them.
Yes, baker. David says, "my cup overflows" (Psalm 23:5). A cup that overflows is a picture of having more than enough. The LORD's care isn't just barely enough for David, it spills over.
Not this one, baker. The text says, "my cup overflows" (Psalm 23:5), and it doesn't say David was careless. The picture is abundance, not a mistake.
Not quite, baker. Verse 5 says, "my cup overflows" (Psalm 23:5), and nothing in the verse says David is being rushed. The picture is a cup full to the brim.
Yes, baker. David says, "Surely goodness and mercy will follow me all the days of my life" (Psalm 23:6). Those are the things that follow David every day of his life.
Not this one, baker. Verse 6 names goodness and mercy as what follows David (Psalm 23:6). Wealth and honor aren't named anywhere in this psalm.
Not quite, baker. The text says, "goodness and mercy will follow me" (Psalm 23:6). Strength and wisdom aren't named there, so look for what the verse says follows David.

explanations.answer: In the house of the LORD
explanations.explanation: Yes, baker. David closes the psalm by saying, "I will dwell in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6). The song ends with David staying in the LORD's house.
Not this one, baker. The psalm names the house of the LORD as the place David will dwell (Psalm 23:6). Hebron doesn't come up in the song at all.
Not quite, baker. Canaan isn't in Psalm 23. David says he will dwell "in the house of the LORD forever" (Psalm 23:6), and that's the only place the text names.
